key_insight: Rescaling classical magnetic transition temperatures by (S+1)/S closely reproduces quantum benchmarks across 17 tested compounds.
engineering_relevance: Reliable magnetic transition-temperature predictions require both accurate exchange energies and quantum-aware spin thermodynamics.
method: Benchmark DMC and DFT magnetic energy differences for five insulating antiferromagnets against INS-derived references.
Compare classical Monte Carlo temperatures with quantum stochastic series expansion results for 17 INS-derived Heisenberg models.
evidence_signal: Rescaling reduced the mean absolute classical–quantum temperature difference from 81.7 to 8.2 K, with a mean absolute percentage difference of 5.9%; DMC energy errors were comparable to those of the best tested functionals.
watch_item: The rescaling is validated within the tested Heisenberg models, not established as universal; DMC also systematically underestimated the energy references.
paper_title: Quantum benchmarks for magnetic energies and transition temperatures
